weeks.title: Types of data
weeks.summary: Data kya hota hai, variables kitne type ke hote hain aur har variable ko sahi category me kaise daalte hain, yeh is week ka base hai. Aage ke saare graphs aur formulas isi classification pe depend karte hain.
concepts: **Variable** ek characteristic hai jo har case ke liye alag value le sakti hai (jaise height, city), aur **data** in values ka recorded collection hai.
Table me har row ek **case / observation** hoti hai aur har column ek **variable**. Pehle hamesha check karo ki ek row kis cheez ko represent karti hai.

**Categorical (qualitative)** variable group ya label batata hai (blood group, state), jabki **numerical (quantitative)** variable ek measured ya counted number hota hai jis pe arithmetic meaningful hai.
**Nominal** categories me koi natural order nahi hota (red, blue, green), lekin **ordinal** categories me order hota hai (low < medium < high), bhale hi gaps equal na hon.
**Discrete** numerical data countable values leta hai (siblings ki ginti), jabki **continuous** data kisi range me koi bhi value le sakta hai (weight, time).
**Interval scale** pe differences meaningful hain par zero arbitrary hai (temperature °C), aur **ratio scale** pe true zero hota hai, isliye 'double' ya 'half' bolna valid hai (weight, income).
**Numbers hamesha numerical nahi hote**: roll number, PIN code, jersey number sirf labels hain, isliye yeh categorical hain.
**Cross-sectional data** ek hi time pe kai cases ka hota hai, aur **time series data** ek hi cheez ko time ke saath baar baar record karta hai (daily share price).

example.problem: Ek class ke dataset me yeh columns hain: Roll No, Gender, Height (cm), Number of siblings, Grade (A/B/C), Home city ka aaj ka temperature (°C). Har variable ka type batao.
steps: Roll No ek number dikhta hai, par iska average nikalna bekaar hai. Yeh sirf identity label hai, isliye **nominal categorical**.
Gender ke categories me koi order nahi hai, isliye **nominal categorical**.
Height kisi bhi decimal value pe ho sakti hai (162.5 cm), isliye **continuous numerical**, aur true zero hone se ratio scale.
Number of siblings sirf 0, 1, 2, ... ho sakta hai, isliye **discrete numerical**.
Grade A > B > C ka order hai par A aur B ka gap measure nahi kar sakte, isliye **ordinal categorical**.
Temperature °C continuous numerical hai, par 0°C ka matlab 'heat nahi' nahi hai, isliye yeh **interval scale** pe hai.
Answer: Roll No aur Gender nominal, Grade ordinal, Siblings discrete, Height continuous (ratio), Temperature continuous (interval).

mistakes: Har number wale column ko numerical maan lena. Pehle socho ki uska average ya difference meaningful hai ya nahi; PIN code ka average koi matlab nahi rakhta.
Ordinal ko numerical samajh lena. Ratings 1 se 5 me order hai, par 4 aur 5 ka gap 1 aur 2 ke gap jaisa ho, yeh zaroori nahi.
Interval scale pe ratio bolna, jaise '30°C, 15°C se double garam hai'. Yeh galat hai kyunki °C ka zero arbitrary hai.
revision: Categorical: nominal (no order) aur ordinal (order hai).
Ratio scale me true zero hota hai, interval scale me nahi.
Label wale numbers (roll no, PIN) categorical hote hain.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa variable ordinal categorical hai?
questions.explanation: T-shirt size me natural order hai: S < M < L < XL, isliye ordinal hai. Blood group, city aur brand me koi 'chhota-bada' order nahi hota, woh nominal hain.

questions.question: Ek football match me score hue goals ki ginti kis type ka variable hai?
questions.explanation: Goals sirf 0, 1, 2, ... ho sakte hain, 2.5 goal nahi hota. Countable values hain, isliye discrete numerical. Continuous tab hota jab beech ki koi bhi value possible hoti.

questions.question: Kisi student ke address ka PIN code (jaise 600036) kis type ka variable hai?
questions.explanation: PIN code sirf ek area ka label hai. Do PIN codes ka average ya difference koi matlab nahi rakhta, isliye yeh nominal categorical hai. Trap: digits dekh kar isko discrete numerical maan lena.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa variable interval scale pe hai (true zero nahi hai)?
questions.explanation: 0°C ka matlab 'koi temperature nahi' nahi hai, yeh bas ek reference point hai, isliye °C interval scale hai. Weight, income aur books ki ginti me 0 ka matlab sach me 'kuch nahi' hai, woh ratio scale hain.

questions.question: Ek dataset me 250 students hain. Har student ke liye name, age, state aur teen subjects (Maths, Stats, English) ke marks alag alag columns me record hain. Is dataset me kitne cases aur kitne variables hain?
questions.explanation: Har student ek row (case) hai, toh 250 cases. Columns: name, age, state, Maths, Stats, English = 6 variables. Trap: 'marks' ko ek hi variable gin lena, jabki teen subjects teen alag columns hain.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Ordinal data ka mean hamesha meaningful hota hai
40 kg, 20 kg ka double hai, kyunki weight ratio scale pe hai
Jersey number 10 wala player, jersey 5 wale se double accha hai
questions.explanation: Weight me true zero hai, isliye ratio ('double') bolna valid hai. °C interval scale hai to ratio galat hai, jersey number sirf label hai, aur ordinal categories ke beech ke gaps equal nahi hote, isliye unka mean hamesha meaningful nahi hota.

weeks.title: Describing categorical data
weeks.summary: Categorical data ko frequency table, bar chart aur pie chart se summarize karna seekhoge. Saath me mode, ordinal data ka median aur misleading graphs pakadna bhi.
concepts: **Frequency** matlab koi category kitni baar aayi; **relative frequency** = frequency / total (n). Saari relative frequencies ka sum 1 hota hai.
**Frequency table** me har category ke saamne uski frequency aur relative frequency (ya %) likhte hain. Yeh har graph ka starting point hai.
**Bar chart** me har category ka ek alag bar hota hai jiski height frequency ke barabar hoti hai; bars ke beech gap rakhte hain kyunki categories alag alag hain.
**Pie chart** me har category ka angle = relative frequency × 360°. Yeh 'whole ka hissa' dikhane ke liye accha hai, par bahut saari categories me padhna mushkil hai.
**Pareto chart** me bars ko descending frequency me lagate hain aur upar cumulative % ki line banate hain, taaki pata chale kaun si kuch categories zyada contribute karti hain.
**Mode** sabse zyada frequency wali category hai. Nominal data ke liye center ka yahi ek sahi measure hai.
Ordinal data ke liye **median** bhi nikal sakte ho: categories ko order me lagao, cumulative count dekho aur beech wali position kis category me padti hai woh batao.
**Misleading graphs**: y-axis 0 se start na ho, 3D pie ho ya bars ki width alag ho, toh chhota farak bhi bahut bada dikhne lagta hai.

example.problem: 40 students se favourite sport poocha gaya: Cricket 18, Football 10, Badminton 8, Chess 4. Relative frequencies, pie chart ke angles aur mode nikalo.
steps: Relative frequency = frequency / 40: Cricket 18/40 = 0.45, Football 10/40 = 0.25, Badminton 8/40 = 0.20, Chess 4/40 = 0.10.
Pie angle = relative frequency × 360°: Cricket 0.45 × 360 = 162°, Football 90°, Badminton 72°, Chess 36°.
Sabse zyada frequency Cricket (18) ki hai, isliye mode = Cricket.

mistakes: Nominal data ka mean ya median nikalne ki koshish karna. 'Average city' jaisa kuch nahi hota; nominal ke liye sirf mode use karo.
Pie chart angle me 360 se multiply karna bhool jaana, ya percentage ko seedha degree maan lena (25% ko 25° likh dena).
Graph ka y-axis check kiye bina conclusion nikalna. Pehle dekho axis 0 se start ho raha hai ya nahi.
revision: Relative frequency = f / n, aur sabka sum = 1.
Nominal: sirf mode. Ordinal: mode aur median dono.
Pareto chart = descending bars + cumulative % line.
Truncated y-axis chhote farak ko bada dikhata hai.

questions.question: Nominal categorical variable (jaise favourite colour) ke center ko batane ke liye sabse sahi measure kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: Nominal categories me na arithmetic possible hai na order, isliye mean aur median nahi nikal sakte. Mode (sabse frequent category) hi kaam karta hai. Standard deviation toh spread ka measure hai, center ka nahi.

questions.question: 50 logon ke survey me 15 logon ne chai ko apna favourite drink bataya. Chai ki relative frequency kya hai?
questions.explanation: Relative frequency = 15 / 50 = 0.30. Option 15 sirf frequency hai, aur 0.15 tab aata jab galti se 100 se divide kar dete.

questions.question: 200 students me se 50 ne Science stream choose kiya. Pie chart me Science ke slice ka angle kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Angle = (50 / 200) × 360° = 0.25 × 360° = 90°. Trap: 25% ko seedha 25° likh dena, ya frequency 50 ko hi degree maan lena.

questions.question: 9 customers ki ratings: Poor 2, Average 3, Good 3, Excellent 1. Is ordinal data ki median category kya hai?
questions.explanation: n = 9, toh median 5th position pe hai. Order me cumulative count: Poor = positions 1-2, Average = 3-5, Good = 6-8, Excellent = 9. 5th position Average me hai. Trap: Good ko median maan lena kyunki uski frequency bhi 3 hai, par median position se nikalta hai, frequency se nahi.

questions.question: Pareto chart me bars kis order me lagaye jaate hain?
options: Category ke naam ke alphabetical order me
Descending frequency, saath me cumulative % ki line
questions.explanation: Pareto chart ka maqsad yeh dikhana hai ki kaun si thodi categories sabse zyada hissa leti hain, isliye bars bade se chhote order me hote hain aur cumulative % line saath me hoti hai. Ascending order ulta hai.

questions.question: Ek bar chart me Brand A ki sales 92 aur Brand B ki 96 hai, par y-axis 0 ki jagah 90 se start hota hai. Graph me B ka bar, A ke bar se dekhne me kitna guna lamba dikhega?
questions.explanation: Axis 90 se start hai, toh dikhne wali heights 92 − 90 = 2 aur 96 − 90 = 6 hain, yaani B ka bar 6 / 2 = 3 guna lamba dikhega. Asli ratio sirf 96 / 92 ≈ 1.04 hai. Isi wajah se truncated axis misleading hota hai.

weeks.title: Describing numerical data
weeks.summary: Numerical data ka center (mean, median, mode) aur spread (range, variance, standard deviation, IQR) nikalna seekhoge. Outliers pakadna aur data shift ya scale karne ka effect bhi samjhoge.
concepts: **Mean** x̄ = Σx / n, sabhi values ka average. Yeh outliers se bahut affect hota hai.
**Median** ke liye pehle data sort karo; n odd ho toh beech wali value, n even ho toh beech ki do values ka average. Yeh outliers se kam affect hota hai.
**Mode** sabse zyada baar aane wali value hai; data me ek se zyada mode bhi ho sakte hain.
**Range** = max − min. **Variance** spread ka measure hai: population ke liye σ² = Σ(x − μ)² / n aur sample ke liye s² = Σ(x − x̄)² / (n − 1). **Standard deviation** = √variance.
**Percentile**: p-th percentile woh value hai jiske neeche lagbhag p% data hota hai. Q1 = 25th, Q2 = median, Q3 = 75th percentile.
**IQR** = Q3 − Q1. Outlier rule: value < Q1 − 1.5 × IQR ya value > Q3 + 1.5 × IQR ho toh outlier.
**Five-number summary** (min, Q1, median, Q3, max) se **box plot** banta hai.
**Shift aur scale**: har value me c add karne se mean c se badhta hai par SD same rehta hai; har value ko a se multiply karne pe mean aur SD dono |a| guna ho jaate hain, aur variance a² guna.

example.problem: Data: 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 8. Mean, median, mode, range, population variance aur sample variance nikalo.
steps: Data pehle se sorted hai. n even hai, toh median = (3rd + 4th) / 2 = (4 + 5) / 2 = 4.5.
4 do baar aaya hai, baaki ek ek baar, toh mode = 4. Range = 8 − 2 = 6.
Mean se deviations: −3, −1, −1, 0, 2, 3. Inke squares: 9, 1, 1, 0, 4, 9, jinka sum = 24.
Answer: mean 5, median 4.5, mode 4, range 6, σ² = 4, s² = 4.8.

mistakes: Median nikalne se pehle data sort karna bhool jaana. Unsorted list ki beech wali value median nahi hoti.
Population aur sample variance mix karna. Question me 'sample' likha ho toh n − 1 se divide karo, warna n se.
Har value me constant add karne pe SD bhi badha dena. Shift se spread nahi badalta, sirf center badalta hai.
revision: Mean = Σx / n; median = sorted data ki beech wali value.
σ² = Σ(x − μ)² / n, s² = Σ(x − x̄)² / (n − 1).
IQR = Q3 − Q1; fences = Q1 − 1.5 IQR aur Q3 + 1.5 IQR.
Y = aX + b ⇒ mean(Y) = a·mean(X) + b, SD(Y) = |a|·SD(X).
Outliers mean ko kheenchte hain, median ko kam.

questions.question: Data 2, 5, 6, 9, 13 ka mean kya hai?
questions.explanation: Sum = 2 + 5 + 6 + 9 + 13 = 35, n = 5, mean = 35 / 5 = 7. Option 6 median hai (beech wali value), aur 35 sirf sum hai.

questions.question: Data 12, 5, 9, 20, 7, 15 ka median kya hai?
questions.explanation: Sort karo: 5, 7, 9, 12, 15, 20. n = 6 even hai, toh median = (9 + 12) / 2 = 10.5. Option 11.33 mean hai (68 / 6), aur 9 ya 12 akele beech ki values hain, median nahi.

questions.question: Ek data ka mean 20 aur standard deviation 4 hai. Har value ko 3 se multiply karke usme 2 add kiya gaya. Naya mean aur naya SD kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Naya mean = 3 × 20 + 2 = 62. SD pe add ka koi asar nahi, sirf multiply ka: 3 × 4 = 12. Trap: SD me bhi 2 add karna (14), ya variance wala a² factor SD pe laga dena (4 × 9 = 36).

questions.question: Data 1, 3, 5, 7 ko poori population maano. Population variance kya hai?
questions.explanation: Mean = 16 / 4 = 4. Deviations −3, −1, 1, 3; squares 9, 1, 1, 9; sum = 20. Population variance = 20 / 4 = 5. Option 6.67 sample variance hai (20 / 3), aur 2.24 standard deviation hai, variance nahi.

questions.question: Ek data ka Q1 = 20 aur Q3 = 35 hai. 1.5 × IQR rule ke hisaab se inme se kaunsi value outlier hai?
questions.explanation: IQR = 35 − 20 = 15. Upper fence = 35 + 1.5 × 15 = 57.5. Sirf 60 is fence se upar hai, toh wahi outlier hai. 57 fence ke bilkul paas hai par 57.5 se kam hai, isliye outlier nahi.

questions.question: 10 numbers ka mean 15 nikla. Baad me pata chala ki ek value 24 galti se 42 likh di gayi thi. Sahi mean kya hai?
questions.explanation: Galat sum = 15 × 10 = 150. Sahi sum = 150 − 42 + 24 = 132. Sahi mean = 132 / 10 = 13.2. Trap 16.8: correction ulti direction me laga dena (150 + 18 = 168).

weeks.title: Association between variables
weeks.summary: Do variables ek doosre se jude hain ya nahi, yeh check karna seekhoge: categorical ke liye two-way table, aur numerical ke liye scatter plot, covariance aur correlation.
concepts: **Two-way (contingency) table** do categorical variables ki frequencies ek saath dikhati hai; rows ek variable ki categories aur columns doosre ki.

**Row / column relative frequency** se conditional proportion milta hai, jaise 'hostel students me pass ka proportion'. Agar har row me yeh proportion lagbhag same hai toh variables me association nahi hai.
**Scatter plot** do numerical variables ko points ki tarah dikhata hai; isse direction (positive/negative), form (linear/curved) aur strength dikhti hai.

**Covariance** = Σ(x − x̄)(y − ȳ) / n (population) ya / (n − 1) (sample). Positive ho toh dono saath badhte hain, negative ho toh ek badhe doosra ghate. Iski unit x aur y ki units ka product hoti hai.
**Correlation coefficient** r = Cov(x, y) / (σx · σy). Yeh unit-free hai aur hamesha −1 ≤ r ≤ 1.
r ≈ ±1 matlab strong **linear** relation, r ≈ 0 matlab linear relation nahi (curved relation phir bhi ho sakta hai).
x ya y ko kisi positive constant se multiply karne ya shift karne pe r **nahi badalta**; negative constant se multiply karo toh sirf sign ulta hota hai.
**Correlation ≠ causation**: ice-cream sales aur doobne ke cases dono garmi me badhte hain, par ek doosre ka kaaran nahi hain.

example.problem: x: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 aur y: 2, 4, 5, 4, 5. Correlation coefficient r nikalo.
steps: r = 6 / √(10 × 6) = 6 / √60 ≈ 6 / 7.746 ≈ 0.77. (n wala factor upar neeche cancel ho jaata hai.)
Answer: r ≈ 0.77, yaani moderately strong positive linear relation.

mistakes: Joint proportion aur conditional proportion mix karna. 'Hostel me pass ka proportion' ke liye hostel wali row ke total se divide karo, poore total se nahi.
r = 0 dekh ke bol dena ki koi relation hi nahi hai. r sirf linear relation naapta hai; U-shape relation me bhi r ≈ 0 aa sakta hai.
Strong correlation ko cause-effect maan lena. Koi teesra variable dono ko chala sakta hai.
revision: Cov(x, y) = Σ(x − x̄)(y − ȳ) / n.
r = Cov(x, y) / (σx σy), aur −1 ≤ r ≤ 1.
Units badalne ya shift karne se r same rehta hai.
Conditional proportion = cell / row (ya column) total.

questions.question: Do variables ka correlation r = −0.9 hai. Iska sabse sahi matlab kya hai?
questions.explanation: Negative sign batata hai ki ek badhe toh doosra ghatta hai, aur |r| = 0.9 jo 1 ke kareeb hai, yaani relation strong aur linear hai. Sign aur magnitude dono alag alag padhna zaroori hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsi value correlation coefficient r ki ho hi nahi sakti?
questions.explanation: r hamesha −1 aur 1 ke beech hota hai. 1.3 is range ke bahar hai, toh impossible hai. 0 aur −1 bilkul valid values hain.

questions.question: 100 students ki table: Hostel me Pass 45, Fail 15. Day scholars me Pass 25, Fail 15. Hostel students me pass hone ka proportion kya hai?
questions.explanation: Hostel row ka total = 45 + 15 = 60. Proportion = 45 / 60 = 0.75. Trap: 45 / 100 = 0.45 joint proportion hai, 70 / 100 = 0.70 overall pass rate hai, aur 25 / 40 = 0.625 day scholars ka hai.

questions.question: Do variables ka covariance 12 hai, x ka SD 3 aur y ka SD 5 hai (sab same divisor se nikale gaye). Correlation r kya hai?
questions.explanation: r = Cov / (σx σy) = 12 / (3 × 5) = 12 / 15 = 0.8. Option 12 sirf covariance hai, aur 4 = 12 / 3 (sirf ek SD se divide karna).

questions.question: Height (x) aur weight (y) ka correlation r nikala gaya. Ab saari heights ko cm se inches me badal diya (2.54 se divide kiya), weight same rakha. Naya r kya hoga?
options: r ko 2.54 se divide karna padega
r ka sign ulta ho jaayega
questions.explanation: r unit-free hai. Positive constant se multiply ya divide karne pe covariance aur SD dono same factor se badalte hain jo cancel ho jaata hai. Sign tab ulta hota jab negative constant se multiply karte.

questions.question: x: 2, 4, 6, 8 aur y: 3, 7, 5, 9. Correlation coefficient r kya hai?
questions.explanation: x̄ = 5, ȳ = 6. Deviations x: −3, −1, 1, 3; y: −3, 1, −1, 3. Products ka sum = 9 − 1 − 1 + 9 = 16. Σdx² = 20, Σdy² = 20. r = 16 / √(20 × 20) = 16 / 20 = 0.8. Trap: 4 population covariance hai (16 / 4), aur 0.64 = r² hai.

weeks.title: Permutations and combinations
weeks.summary: Ginti karne ke basic rules seekhoge: addition aur multiplication principle, factorial, permutations aur combinations. Yahi probability calculate karne ka foundation hai.
concepts: **Addition rule**: agar ek kaam A tareekon se ya B tareekon se ho sakta hai (dono saath nahi), toh total A + B tareeke.
**Multiplication rule**: agar pehla step m tareekon se aur doosra step n tareekon se ho, toh dono steps milake m × n tareeke.
**Factorial** n! = n × (n − 1) × ... × 1, aur 0! = 1. n alag cheezon ko line me lagane ke n! tareeke hain.
**Permutation** (order matter karta hai): nPr = n! / (n − r)!. Jaise 1st, 2nd, 3rd prize dena.
**Combination** (order matter nahi karta): nCr = n! / (r! (n − r)!). Jaise team ya committee choose karna. Hamesha nPr = nCr × r!.
**Repetition allowed**: har position pe n choices ho aur r positions, toh n^r tareeke (jaise PIN code).
**Identical objects**: n cheezein jisme p ek jaisi aur q ek jaisi hain, toh arrangements = n! / (p! q!).
**Circular arrangement**: n log gol table pe = (n − 1)! tareeke, kyunki rotation se arrangement nahi badalta.

example.problem: 6 ladke aur 4 ladkiyon me se 3 ladke aur 2 ladkiyon ki committee kitne tareekon se ban sakti hai?
steps: Committee me order matter nahi karta, isliye combinations use karenge.
Dono choices ek saath karni hain, toh multiplication rule: 20 × 6.

mistakes: Permutation aur combination me confuse hona. Khud se poocho: kya A-B aur B-A alag gine jaayenge? Haan toh permutation, nahi toh combination.
'At least one' wale sawalon me ek item fix karke baaki free choose karna, jisse double counting hoti hai. Iske jagah total − (none) use karo.
Repeated letters wale words me identical letters ke factorial se divide karna bhool jaana.
revision: nPr = n! / (n − r)!, nCr = n! / (r!(n − r)!).

questions.question: Ek student ke paas 3 shirts aur 4 pants hain. Ek shirt aur ek pant pehenne ke kitne alag outfits ban sakte hain?
questions.explanation: Pehle shirt choose karo (3 tareeke), phir pant (4 tareeke). Multiplication rule se 3 × 4 = 12. Trap: 3 + 4 = 7 addition rule tab lagta jab sirf ek item choose karna hota.

questions.question: 5C2 ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: 5C2 = 5! / (2! × 3!) = 120 / (2 × 6) = 10. Option 20 = 5P2 hai, jisme order count hota hai; combination me usko 2! se divide karte hain.

questions.question: 6 dost ek gol table ke chaaron taraf kitne tareekon se baith sakte hain (sirf rotation se bane arrangements same maane jaayenge)?
questions.explanation: Circular arrangement = (6 − 1)! = 5! = 120. 720 = 6! line wala answer hai, rotation ko alag gina. 360 tab aata jab clockwise aur anticlockwise ko bhi same maante (jaise necklace), jo yahan nahi kaha gaya.

questions.question: 'BANANA' word ke letters ko kitne alag tareekon se arrange kar sakte hain?
questions.explanation: 6 letters: A teen baar, N do baar, B ek baar. Arrangements = 6! / (3! × 2!) = 720 / 12 = 60. Trap: sirf 3! se divide karna (120) ya sirf 2! se (360); dono repeated letters ka dhyan rakhna hai.

questions.question: Ek 4-digit PIN me har digit 0 se 9 tak kuch bhi ho sakta hai aur digits repeat ho sakte hain. Kitne alag PIN possible hain?
questions.explanation: Har position pe 10 choices, 4 positions: 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 10⁴ = 10000. 5040 = 10P4 tab hota jab repetition allowed nahi hoti.

questions.question: 5 men aur 4 women me se 4 logon ki committee banani hai jisme kam se kam 1 woman ho. Kitne tareeke hain?
questions.explanation: Total committees = 9C4 = 126. Bina kisi woman ke (sirf men) = 5C4 = 5. At least one woman = 126 − 5 = 121. Trap 224: pehle ek woman fix karna (4 tareeke) aur baaki 3 kisi bhi 8 me se (8C3 = 56), 4 × 56 = 224, jo same committee ko kai baar ginta hai.

weeks.title: Probability basics
weeks.summary: Experiment, sample space aur events ki language seekhoge, aur classical probability, complement aur union (addition) rule se probability nikaloge.
concepts: **Random experiment** woh process hai jiska result pehle se pakka nahi pata (coin toss, die roll). Saare possible outcomes ka set **sample space** S hai.
**Event** sample space ka ek subset hai, jaise 'die pe even number' = {2, 4, 6}.
**Classical probability**: jab saare outcomes equally likely hon, P(A) = (A ke favourable outcomes) / (total outcomes).
**Axioms**: 0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1, P(S) = 1, aur mutually exclusive events ke liye P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).
**Complement rule**: P(A') = 1 − P(A). 'At least one' wale sawalon me yeh bahut kaam aata hai.
**Addition rule**: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). Common part do baar gina jaata hai, isliye ek baar ghatate hain.
**Mutually exclusive** events ek saath nahi ho sakte, yaani P(A ∩ B) = 0.
Do dice ke sawal me sample space ke 36 **ordered** outcomes lo, jaise (2, 5) aur (5, 2) alag hain; tabhi saare outcomes equally likely rehte hain.

example.problem: Do fair dice phenke gaye. Kam se kam ek six aane ki probability kya hai?
steps: Sample space me 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely ordered outcomes hain.
'Kam se kam ek six' seedha ginna lamba hai, toh complement lo: 'koi six nahi'.
Koi six nahi matlab dono dice pe 1 se 5: 5 × 5 = 25 outcomes. P(koi six nahi) = 25 / 36.
Check: seedha gino toh pehle die pe six (6) + doosre pe six (6) − dono six (1) = 11. Same answer: 11 / 36.

mistakes: Union rule me P(A ∩ B) ghatana bhool jaana. Aisa karne se probability 1 se bhi upar ja sakti hai.
Do dice ke sums ko equally likely maan lena. Sum 7 ke 6 tareeke hain par sum 2 ka sirf 1, isliye 36 ordered outcomes se gino.
Mutually exclusive aur independent ko same samajhna. Mutually exclusive events (non-zero probability wale) kabhi independent nahi hote.
revision: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).

questions.question: Ek coin 3 baar toss kiya gaya. Sample space me kitne outcomes hain?
questions.explanation: Har toss ke 2 outcomes, 3 tosses: 2 × 2 × 2 = 2³ = 8 (HHH, HHT, ..., TTT). Trap: 3 × 2 = 6 karna, jo multiplication rule ko galat lagana hai.

questions.question: P(A) = 0.35 hai. P(A') (A ka complement) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(A') = 1 − P(A) = 1 − 0.35 = 0.65. 1.35 probability ho hi nahi sakti kyunki woh 1 se zyada hai.

questions.question: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 aur P(A ∩ B) = 0.2 hai. P(A ∪ B) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(A ∪ B) = 0.5 + 0.4 − 0.2 = 0.7. Trap: intersection ghatana bhool ke 0.9 likh dena; common part do baar gin jaata hai.

questions.question: Do fair dice phenke gaye. Dono numbers ka sum 8 aane ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Sum 8 wale ordered outcomes: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2) = 5. P = 5 / 36. Trap 5/11: possible sums (2 se 12) ko 11 equally likely outcomes maan lena, jo galat hai.

questions.question: 52 cards ki deck se ek card nikala. Card king ya heart hone ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(king) = 4/52, P(heart) = 13/52, P(king of hearts) = 1/52. P = 4/52 + 13/52 − 1/52 = 16/52 = 4/13. Trap 17/52: king of hearts ko do baar gin lena.

questions.question: Ek bag me 5 red aur 3 blue balls hain. Bina wapas daale (without replacement) 2 balls nikali gayi. Dono balls same colour ki hone ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Total tareeke = 8C2 = 28. Dono red = 5C2 = 10, dono blue = 3C2 = 3. P = (10 + 3) / 28 = 13/28. Traps: 15/28 alag colour wali probability hai (5 × 3), 5/14 = 10/28 sirf dono red hai, aur 17/32 with-replacement wala answer hai (25 + 9) / 64.

weeks.title: Conditional probability and Bayes
weeks.summary: Jab kuch information pehle se pata ho tab probability kaise update hoti hai, yeh seekhoge: conditional probability, independence, total probability aur Bayes theorem.
concepts: **Conditional probability**: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B), jahan P(B) > 0. Matlab B ho chuka hai, ab sample space sirf B tak simit hai.
**Multiplication rule**: P(A ∩ B) = P(B) × P(A | B). Without replacement wale draws me step by step multiply karte hain.
**Independent events**: P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B), yaani B ke hone se A ki probability nahi badalti: P(A | B) = P(A).
**Independent vs mutually exclusive**: mutually exclusive me P(A ∩ B) = 0; agar dono ki probability positive hai toh woh independent nahi ho sakte.
**Law of total probability**: agar B₁, B₂, ... poore sample space ko baant dete hain, toh P(A) = Σ P(Bᵢ) P(A | Bᵢ).
**Bayes theorem**: P(Bᵢ | A) = P(Bᵢ) P(A | Bᵢ) / P(A). Isse 'effect dekh ke cause ki probability' nikalte hain.
**Base rate** ka dhyan rakho: rare disease ka test positive aane pe bhi actual disease ki probability kaafi kam ho sakti hai.

example.problem: Ek disease 1% logon ko hai. Test disease wale logon me 95% baar positive aata hai, aur healthy logon me 5% baar galti se positive aata hai. Kisi ka test positive aaya. Use sach me disease hone ki probability kya hai?
steps: D = disease hai, + = test positive. Given: P(D) = 0.01, P(+ | D) = 0.95, P(+ | D') = 0.05.
Answer: sirf lagbhag 16%. Disease rare hai, isliye zyada positives healthy logon ke false positives hain.

mistakes: P(A | B) aur P(B | A) ko same samajhna. P(+ | D) = 0.95 ka matlab P(D | +) = 0.95 nahi hai.
Without replacement draws me doosre draw ki probability update na karna (denominator ek kam karna bhool jaana).
Total probability me sirf conditional probabilities ka simple average le lena, unke weights (P(Bᵢ)) bhool ke.
revision: P(Bᵢ | A) = P(Bᵢ) P(A | Bᵢ) / P(A).

questions.question: P(A ∩ B) = 0.12 aur P(B) = 0.4 hai. P(A | B) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B) = 0.12 / 0.4 = 0.3. Trap 0.048: divide ki jagah multiply kar dena (0.12 × 0.4).

questions.question: A aur B independent events hain, P(A) = 0.5 aur P(B) = 0.6. P(A ∩ B) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Independent events ke liye P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B) = 0.5 × 0.6 = 0.3. Option 0 tab hota jab events mutually exclusive hote, independent nahi.

questions.question: Ek fair die phenka gaya aur bataya gaya ki number even aaya hai. Number 3 se bada hone ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Even diya hai, toh naya sample space {2, 4, 6}. Inme 3 se bade: {4, 6}. P = 2/3. Trap 1/2: condition ignore karke P(X > 3) = 3/6 likh dena.

questions.question: Ek bag me 4 red aur 6 blue balls hain. Bina wapas daale 2 balls nikali. Dono red hone ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(pehli red) = 4/10, phir 3 red aur 9 total bache: P(doosri red | pehli red) = 3/9. P = 4/10 × 3/9 = 12/90 = 2/15. Trap 4/25: with replacement maan ke (4/10)² nikalna.

questions.question: Ek factory me Machine A 60% items banati hai jisme 2% defective hote hain, aur Machine B 40% items banati hai jisme 5% defective hote hain. Random item defective hone ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Total probability: P(D) = 0.6 × 0.02 + 0.4 × 0.05 = 0.012 + 0.020 = 0.032. Trap 0.035: 2% aur 5% ka simple average lena, jabki machines ka share alag hai.

questions.question: Machine A 60% items banati hai (2% defective) aur Machine B 40% items (5% defective). Ek random item defective nikla. Woh Machine B se bana ho, iski probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(D) = 0.012 + 0.020 = 0.032. Bayes: P(B | D) = 0.020 / 0.032 = 0.625. Trap 0.4: sirf B ka production share batana; 0.375 = P(A | D) hai.

weeks.title: Random variables
weeks.summary: Random variable kya hota hai, discrete random variable ka PMF aur CDF kaise likhte hain, aur unse probabilities kaise padhte hain, yeh is week me seekhoge.
concepts: **Random variable** (RV) ek function hai jo har outcome ko ek number deta hai, jaise 'do coins me heads ki ginti'.
**Discrete RV** countable values leta hai (0, 1, 2, ...), aur **continuous RV** kisi interval me koi bhi value le sakta hai.
**PMF** (probability mass function) p(x) = P(X = x). Valid PMF ke liye har p(x) ≥ 0 aur Σ p(x) = 1.
**CDF** F(x) = P(X ≤ x). Yeh kabhi ghatta nahi, 0 se start hokar 1 tak jaata hai, aur discrete RV ke liye steps me badhta hai.
CDF se PMF: discrete RV ke liye P(X = x) = F(x) − (x se just pehle ki F value), yaani jump ka size.
**Bernoulli RV**: sirf 0 ya 1 value, P(X = 1) = p. Ek trial ka success/failure isse model hota hai.
**Discrete uniform**: n values, har ek ki probability 1/n, jaise fair die.

example.problem: Do fair coins toss kiye. X = heads ki ginti. X ka PMF aur CDF likho.
steps: Sample space: HH, HT, TH, TT, sab equally likely (har ek 1/4).
X = 1 pe HT aur TH: P(X = 1) = 2/4 = 1/2.
CDF: F(x) = 0 jab x < 0; 1/4 jab 0 ≤ x < 1; 3/4 jab 1 ≤ x < 2; aur 1 jab x ≥ 2.

mistakes: PMF ka sum 1 hai ya nahi, yeh check na karna. Unknown constant (k) wale sawalon me isi condition se k nikalta hai.
CDF ki value ko seedha P(X = x) maan lena. F(x) cumulative hai; P(X = x) ke liye jump dekho.
P(X < 2) aur P(X ≤ 2) ko discrete RV me same maan lena. Discrete me P(X = 2) positive ho sakta hai, isliye dono alag ho sakte hain.
revision: CDF: F(x) = P(X ≤ x), non-decreasing, 0 se 1.
P(X = a) = F(a) − F(a se just pehle).

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa valid PMF hai?
questions.explanation: Valid PMF me har value ≥ 0 aur sum = 1 hona chahiye. 0.2 + 0.8 = 1, sahi. Pehle me sum 1.1, doosre me 0.6, aur chauthe me negative probability hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa discrete random variable hai?
options: Bus ke liye wait karne ka time
Ek din me website pe aaye visitors ki ginti
questions.explanation: Visitors ki ginti 0, 1, 2, ... jaisi countable values leti hai, isliye discrete. Height, time aur baarish measure hote hain aur beech ki koi bhi value le sakte hain, isliye continuous.

questions.question: X ka PMF: P(X=1) = k, P(X=2) = 2k, P(X=3) = 3k, P(X=4) = 4k. k ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Sum = 1 hona chahiye: k + 2k + 3k + 4k = 10k = 1, toh k = 0.1. Trap 0.25: 4 values dekh ke 1/4 maan lena, jabki probabilities equal nahi hain.

questions.question: X ka PMF: P(X=1) = 0.1, P(X=2) = 0.2, P(X=3) = 0.3, P(X=4) = 0.4. CDF ki value F(2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: F(2) = P(X ≤ 2) = P(X=1) + P(X=2) = 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3. Trap 0.2: CDF ko PMF samajh ke sirf P(X = 2) likh dena.

questions.question: Do fair dice phenke gaye. X = dono numbers me se bada number (maximum). P(X = 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Max = 2 ke liye dono numbers ≤ 2 hon aur kam se kam ek 2 ho: (1,2), (2,1), (2,2) = 3 outcomes. P = 3/36 = 1/12. Trap 2/36: (2,2) ko bhool jaana.

questions.question: Discrete RV X ka CDF: F(x) = 0 (x < 0), 0.2 (0 ≤ x < 1), 0.5 (1 ≤ x < 2), 0.9 (2 ≤ x < 3), 1 (x ≥ 3). P(X = 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(X = 2) = x = 2 pe CDF ka jump = 0.9 − 0.5 = 0.4. Trap 0.9: F(2) ko hi P(X = 2) maan lena; 0.1 = P(X = 3) hai.

weeks.title: Expectation and variance
weeks.summary: Random variable ka expected value (long-run average) aur variance nikalna seekhoge, aur linear transformations aur sums pe inke rules use karoge.
concepts: **Expectation** E[X] = Σ x · P(X = x). Yeh experiment ko bahut baar repeat karne pe milne wala average hai; yeh zaroori nahi ki X ki koi possible value ho.
**Linearity**: E[aX + b] = a E[X] + b, aur hamesha E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y] (independence ki zaroorat nahi).
**Function ka expectation**: E[g(X)] = Σ g(x) · P(X = x), jaise E[X²] = Σ x² · P(X = x).
**Variance** Var(X) = E[(X − μ)²] = E[X²] − (E[X])². Yeh hamesha ≥ 0 hota hai.
**Standard deviation** SD(X) = √Var(X), jo X ki unit me hota hai.
**Var(aX + b) = a² Var(X)**: constant add karne se spread nahi badalta, aur a ka sign square me chala jaata hai.
Agar X aur Y **independent** hain toh Var(X + Y) = Var(X − Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y). Variances hamesha add hote hain, subtract nahi.

example.problem: X ki values 0, 1, 2 hain probabilities 0.2, 0.5, 0.3 ke saath. E[X], Var(X) aur SD nikalo.

mistakes: (E[X])² aur E[X²] ko same samajhna. Pehle har x ko square karo, phir probability se multiply karo.
Var(aX + b) me b add kar dena ya a ko square na karna. Sahi: sirf a², b ka koi role nahi.
Independent X, Y ke liye Var(X − Y) = Var(X) − Var(Y) likh dena. Variance hamesha add hota hai.
revision: Independent: Var(aX + bY) = a² Var(X) + b² Var(Y).

questions.question: Ek fair die ke outcome X ka expected value E[X] kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[X] = (1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6) / 6 = 21 / 6 = 3.5. Expected value ka possible outcome hona zaroori nahi. 21 sirf sum hai.

questions.question: E[X] = 4 hai. E[3X − 2] kya hai?
questions.explanation: Linearity se E[3X − 2] = 3 × 4 − 2 = 10. Trap 14: minus ko plus padh lena (3 × 4 + 2), aur 12 = constant ko bhool jaana.

questions.question: Var(X) = 4 hai. Var(−2X + 5) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var(aX + b) = a² Var(X) = (−2)² × 4 = 16. Constant 5 ka koi asar nahi. Trap −8: a ko square na karna; variance kabhi negative nahi hota.

questions.question: X ki values 1, 2, 3 hain probabilities 0.5, 0.3, 0.2 ke saath. Var(X) kya hai?
Ek game me ₹10 dekar ek fair die phenkte ho. Six aaye toh ₹30 milte hain, warna kuch nahi. Ek game me expected net gain kya hai?
questions.explanation: Expected winning = 30 × 1/6 = ₹5. Entry fee ₹10 hai, toh net = 5 − 10 = −₹5. Lambe samay me har game me average ₹5 ka nuksaan. Trap ₹5: fee ghatana bhool jaana.

questions.question: X aur Y independent hain, Var(X) = 3 aur Var(Y) = 5. Var(2X − Y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var(2X − Y) = 2² Var(X) + (−1)² Var(Y) = 4 × 3 + 5 = 17. Trap 7: Y ka variance ghatana (12 − 5); trap 11: 2 ko square na karna (6 + 5).

weeks.title: Binomial and Poisson
weeks.summary: Common discrete distributions seekhoge: Bernoulli, Binomial, Poisson aur Geometric. Kab kaunsa use karna hai aur unke mean aur variance bhi.
concepts: **Bernoulli(p)**: ek trial, success = 1 probability p ke saath. Mean = p, variance = p(1 − p).
**Binomial(n, p)**: n independent trials, har trial me success probability p same, X = successes ki ginti. P(X = k) = nCk · pᵏ · (1 − p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ.
Binomial ka **mean = np** aur **variance = np(1 − p)**.
**Poisson(λ)**: ek fixed time ya area me rare events ki ginti (jaise ek ghante me calls). P(X = k) = e^(−λ) λᵏ / k!.
Poisson me **mean = variance = λ**. Jab n bada aur p chhota ho, Binomial ≈ Poisson(λ = np).
**Geometric(p)**: pehla success kis trial pe aata hai. P(X = k) = (1 − p)ᵏ⁻¹ p, aur mean = 1/p.
Binomial ki conditions yaad rakho: fixed n, sirf do outcomes, trials independent, aur har trial me same p.

example.problem: Ek fair coin 5 baar toss kiya. Exactly 3 heads aane ki probability, aur heads ki ginti ka mean aur variance nikalo.
steps: X ~ Binomial(n = 5, p = 0.5), kyunki 5 independent trials hain aur har baar P(head) = 0.5.

mistakes: Binomial formula me nCk lagana bhool jaana. pᵏ(1 − p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ sirf ek particular order ki probability hai.
'At least one' ko 'exactly one' samajh lena. At least one = 1 − P(X = 0).
Binomial mean aur variance mix karna: np mean hai, np(1 − p) variance.
revision: Binomial: P(X = k) = nCk pᵏ (1 − p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ, mean np, var np(1 − p).
Poisson: P(X = k) = e^(−λ) λᵏ / k!, mean = var = λ.
Geometric: P(X = k) = (1 − p)ᵏ⁻¹ p, mean 1/p.
Bernoulli: mean p, var p(1 − p).

questions.question: X ~ Binomial(n = 20, p = 0.3). E[X] kya hai?
questions.explanation: Mean = np = 20 × 0.3 = 6. Trap 4.2: yeh variance hai, np(1 − p) = 20 × 0.3 × 0.7.

questions.question: X ~ Poisson(λ = 4). Var(X) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Poisson me mean aur variance dono λ ke barabar hain, toh Var(X) = 4. Trap 2: standard deviation (√4) ko variance samajh lena; 16 = λ² galat hai.

questions.question: X ~ Binomial(n = 4, p = 0.5). P(X = 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(X = 2) = 4C2 × 0.5² × 0.5² = 6 × 1/16 = 6/16 = 3/8. Trap 1/16: 4C2 lagana bhool jaana; trap 1/2: '4 me se 2 aadha hai' sochna.

questions.question: Ek helpline pe har minute me aane wali calls Poisson(λ = 2) hain. Kisi minute me ek bhi call na aane ki probability kya hai? (e⁻² ≈ 0.135)
Har attempt me success ki probability 0.2 hai aur attempts independent hain. Pehla success exactly 3rd attempt pe aane ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Geometric: pehle do fail, phir success = 0.8 × 0.8 × 0.2 = 0.128. Trap 0.488: yeh 1 − 0.8³ hai, yaani 'pehle 3 attempts me kabhi bhi success'. Trap 0.032: success aur fail ki probability ulti laga dena (0.2² × 0.8).

questions.question: Ek test me 5 MCQs hain, har ek me 4 options aur ek sahi answer. Student har question me random guess karta hai. Kam se kam ek answer sahi hone ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: X ~ Binomial(5, 1/4). P(koi sahi nahi) = (3/4)⁵ = 243/1024. P(at least one) = 1 − 243/1024 = 781/1024 ≈ 0.763. Traps: 243/1024 sirf 'none' hai, aur 405/1024 'exactly one' hai (5 × 1/4 × (3/4)⁴).

weeks.title: Continuous random variables
weeks.summary: Continuous random variable ke liye PDF, area ke roop me probability, CDF aur do important distributions (Uniform aur Exponential) seekhoge.
concepts: **PDF** f(x) continuous RV ka density curve hai. Har jagah f(x) ≥ 0 aur curve ke neeche ka total area = 1.
**Probability = area**: P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = a se b tak f(x) ke neeche ka area. f(x) khud probability nahi hai, isliye 1 se bada bhi ho sakta hai.
Continuous RV ke liye **P(X = a) = 0**, isliye P(X < a) aur P(X ≤ a) same hote hain.
**CDF** F(x) = P(X ≤ x) = x tak ka area; P(a < X < b) = F(b) − F(a).
**Uniform(a, b)**: f(x) = 1 / (b − a) for a ≤ x ≤ b. Mean = (a + b) / 2, variance = (b − a)² / 12.
**Exponential(λ)**: waiting time model, f(x) = λe^(−λx) for x ≥ 0. P(X > x) = e^(−λx), mean = 1/λ.
Exponential **memoryless** hai: P(X > s + t | X > s) = P(X > t). Jitna wait ho chuka, usse aage ka wait affect nahi hota.

example.problem: Bus 0 se 20 minute ke beech kabhi bhi uniformly aati hai. Wait 15 minute se zyada hone ki probability, aur waiting time ka mean aur variance nikalo.
steps: X ~ Uniform(0, 20), toh f(x) = 1/20 jab 0 ≤ x ≤ 20.
Answer: P(X > 15) = 0.25, mean 10 min, variance ≈ 33.33 min².

mistakes: f(x) ki value ko probability samajh lena. Continuous me probability hamesha area hai, ek point pe probability 0 hoti hai.
Triangle ya kisi shape wale PDF me area ka formula galat lagana (triangle me ½ × base × height ka ½ bhool jaana).
Exponential me λ aur mean ko mix karna. Mean 5 hai toh λ = 1/5 = 0.2, na ki 5.
revision: Total area under f(x) = 1, aur P(X = a) = 0.
Uniform(a, b): f = 1/(b − a), mean (a + b)/2, var (b − a)²/12.

questions.question: X ek continuous random variable hai. P(X = 5) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Continuous RV me ek single point ke neeche ka area zero hota hai, isliye P(X = 5) = 0. Trap f(5): density ki value probability nahi hoti. 0.5 bhi galat hai, ek point ke neeche koi area hi nahi hota.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(2, 10). PDF ki height f(x) (2 ≤ x ≤ 10 ke liye) kya hai?
questions.explanation: f(x) = 1 / (b − a) = 1 / (10 − 2) = 1/8, taaki rectangle ka area 8 × 1/8 = 1 ho. Trap 1/10: sirf upper limit se divide karna.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(0, 12). P(3 < X < 7) kya hai?
Ek PDF f(x) = c·x hai jab 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, aur baaki jagah 0. Constant c ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Graph ek triangle hai: base 2, height f(2) = 2c. Area = ½ × 2 × 2c = 2c = 1, toh c = 1/2. Trap 1/4: triangle area me ½ bhool jaana (2 × 2c = 4c = 1).

questions.question: Customer ke aane ka waiting time Exponential hai jiska mean 5 minute hai. Wait 5 minute se zyada hone ki probability kya hai? (e⁻¹ ≈ 0.368)
questions.explanation: Mean 5 hai toh λ = 1/5 = 0.2. P(X > 5) = e^(−0.2 × 5) = e^(−1) ≈ 0.368. Trap 0.5: mean ko median maan lena; exponential symmetric nahi hai. 0.632 = P(X ≤ 5) hai.

questions.question: Ek bulb ki life Exponential hai jiska mean 1000 ghante hai. Bulb 500 ghante chal chuka hai. Woh aur 1000 ghante chalne ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Exponential memoryless hai: P(X > 1500 | X > 500) = P(X > 1000) = e^(−1000/1000) = e^(−1) ≈ 0.368. Trap e^(−1.5): yeh P(X > 1500) hai, jo condition ko ignore karta hai.

weeks.title: Normal distribution
weeks.summary: Bell-shaped Normal distribution, uske parameters μ aur σ, 68-95-99.7 rule aur z-score se standard normal table use karke probabilities nikalna seekhoge.
concepts: **Normal distribution** N(μ, σ²) ek symmetric bell-shaped curve hai jiska center μ pe hai; σ batata hai curve kitna phaila hua hai.
Normal me **mean = median = mode = μ**, aur curve μ ke dono taraf mirror image hota hai.
**Empirical rule (68-95-99.7)**: lagbhag 68% data μ ± σ me, 95% μ ± 2σ me, aur 99.7% μ ± 3σ me hota hai.
**z-score** z = (x − μ) / σ batata hai ki x mean se kitne SD door hai. Isse koi bhi normal **standard normal** Z ~ N(0, 1) ban jaata hai.
**Φ(z)** = P(Z ≤ z), standard normal table se milta hai. Symmetry se Φ(−z) = 1 − Φ(z) aur P(Z > z) = 1 − Φ(z).
**Linear transform**: agar X normal hai toh aX + b bhi normal hai, mean aμ + b aur SD |a|σ ke saath.
**Reverse problem** (cutoff nikalna): pehle table se z dhundo, phir x = μ + zσ.

example.problem: Exam ke marks N(μ = 60, σ = 10) follow karte hain. Random student ke 75 se zyada marks aane ki probability kya hai? (Φ(1.5) = 0.9332)
steps: Answer: lagbhag 6.68% students ke 75 se zyada marks hain.

mistakes: z-score me variance se divide kar dena. Agar σ² = 25 diya hai toh σ = 5 se divide karo, 25 se nahi.
'Greater than' wale sawal me 1 − Φ(z) karna bhool jaana. Table hamesha left side ka area (P(Z ≤ z)) deta hai.
Top 5% cutoff ke liye 1.96 use karna. 1.96 two-sided 95% ke liye hai; one-sided top 5% ke liye 1.645 lagta hai.

questions.question: Normal distribution me mean, median aur mode ke beech kya relation hai?
options: Mode hamesha sabse bada hota hai
questions.explanation: Normal curve μ ke around perfectly symmetric hai, isliye peak (mode), beech wala point (median) aur average (mean) teeno μ pe hote hain. Mean > median > mode right-skewed data me hota hai.

questions.question: Empirical rule ke hisaab se normal data ka lagbhag kitna hissa μ − 2σ aur μ + 2σ ke beech hota hai?
Heights N(μ = 165 cm, σ = 5 cm) follow karti hain. 177 cm height ka z-score kya hai?
questions.explanation: z = (177 − 165) / 5 = 12 / 5 = 2.4. Height mean se upar hai toh z positive hoga. Trap 12: σ se divide karna bhool jaana.

questions.question: X ~ N(μ = 50, σ = 8). Empirical rule se P(42 < X < 66) lagbhag kitna hai?
questions.explanation: 42 = μ − σ aur 66 = μ + 2σ. μ − σ se μ tak = 68% / 2 = 34%, aur μ se μ + 2σ tak = 95% / 2 = 47.5%. Total = 34 + 47.5 = 81.5%. Trap: sirf ek side (68% ya 95%) le lena.

questions.question: Z standard normal hai aur Φ(1) = 0.8413. P(Z > −1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Symmetry se P(Z > −1) = P(Z < 1) = Φ(1) = 0.8413. Trap 0.1587: yeh P(Z > 1) hai; 0.6826 = P(−1 < Z < 1) hai. Probability kabhi negative nahi hoti.

questions.question: Marks N(μ = 70, σ = 10) follow karte hain. Top 5% students ko A grade milta hai. A grade ka minimum cutoff kya hai? (Φ(1.645) = 0.95, Φ(1.96) = 0.975)
questions.explanation: Top 5% matlab cutoff ke neeche 95% area: Φ(z) = 0.95, toh z = 1.645. Cutoff = 70 + 1.645 × 10 = 86.45. Trap 89.6: 1.96 use karna, jo top 2.5% ka cutoff hai. Trap 90: 2σ ko 5% maan lena.
